handoff.failedBody: Your IDEM session could not be confirmed. Sign in to continue.

list.heading: Simulations
list.description: Each simulation puts a project under strain: it looks for the factors that can influence it, runs scenarios, and finds where the model breaks.

empty.heading: No simulations yet
empty.body: Pick an IDEM project or import your business plan. The simulator first shows what it knows about your project, before anything is billed.

newRun.title: New simulation
newRun.heading: New simulation
newRun.description: Three steps: choose the project, review what the engine knows about it, then confirm the simulation level.

source.projectBody: The business plan, market analysis and financial forecasts are already available. Reduced price.
source.importBody: Import your business plan. The engine extracts the activity, market, business model and costs — and creates the matching IDEM project.
source.noProjects: No IDEM project is available on this account.
source.formats: PDF, Word (.docx) or Markdown — 20 MB max
source.signInHeading: Sign in to see your projects
source.signInBody: Listing your IDEM projects needs your account. You can also import a business plan without one, and sign in when it is time to run the analysis.
source.unsupportedFormat: Unsupported format. Import your business plan as PDF, Word (.docx) or Markdown (.md).

newRun.analysingBody: The engine builds a structured picture of the project before simulating anything.
newRun.knowledgeBody: Before simulating, the engine separates what is established from what it has to research, what stays uncertain, and what is missing. That split drives how much confidence the results carry.
newRun.fillGapsBody: Optional, but every answer narrows the uncertainty in the scenarios.

plan.heading: Simulation level
plan.body: Simulation is billed separately from the rest of IDEM: it spends external research, several agents and compute. The amount is confirmed before anything starts.
plan.idemDiscount: Reduced price applied: this project comes from IDEM, so the engine already has its deliverables.
plan.betaBody: Simulation spends external research, several agents and compute. During the beta, IDEM covers that cost.
plan.betaNotice: Whichever level you pick, this simulation will not be billed. The prices shown will apply once the beta ends.

hero.heading: Put your project under strain before you launch it.
hero.subheading: The engine looks for the factors that can tip your business over, stress-tests them, and tells you where your model breaks. Start from what you already have.
hero.note: A simulation is a decision-support tool, never a prediction. Every result comes with how confident the engine is.

tierBody.run: The scenarios, the deciding factors and the viability index.
tierBody.report: The detailed analysis and recommendations, for a simulation already run.
tierBody.pack: The simulation and its full report, cheaper than buying both separately.

includes.scenarios: Scenarios, stress tests and breaking points
includes.index: Viability index, robustness and confidence level

run.title: Simulation running
run.description: The run continues if you close this page. You will be taken to the results as soon as they are ready.
run.failedBody: Nothing is charged for a run that does not finish. Start it again from the list.
run.body: The analysis runs several agents and takes a few minutes. You can close this screen — the run continues.

knowledgeHint.known: Information supplied directly in the project.
knowledgeHint.researchable: External data the engine will collect to make the simulation more realistic.
knowledgeHint.uncertain: No sufficiently reliable data exists. The engine works from an assumption and says so.
knowledgeHint.missing: Parameters that can move the results substantially and remain unknown.

result.indexMeaning: This index measures how robust the project is across the scenarios that were run. It is not a prediction of success.
result.uncertaintiesHint: A high index with wide uncertainty is not the same result as the same index backed by solid data.
result.factorsBody: {{total}} factors were found to be potentially relevant to this project, then ranked by the impact they can have.
result.scenariosBody: {{total}} scenarios were run. The model does not hold in {{broken}} of them.

results.title: Results
results.reportFailed: The report could not be generated
results.notReady: Results for this simulation are not available yet.

upsell.heading: Understand why these scenarios appear
upsell.body: The full report sets out the assumptions used, the sensitivity analysis, the conditions viability depends on, and the recommendations worth acting on first.

factorTierHint.critical: Very high potential impact on the simulated results.
factorTierHint.important: Significant impact, without deciding the outcome on its own.
factorTierHint.secondary: Limited impact across the scenarios that were run.
factorTierHint.unknown: Not enough information to estimate the impact reliably.

report.title: Report
report.heading: Simulation report — {{name}}
report.unavailableBody: This report has not been generated for this simulation yet.

section.validation: To validate in the real world

factors.body: {{total}} factors were kept as potentially relevant to this project, then ranked by the impact they can have on the results.

financials.body: These figures are projections from the simulated scenarios, not guaranteed forecasts.

sensitivity.body: What each move actually changes on the viability index, with every other factor held steady.
sensitivity.unit: Change expressed in viability index points.

conditions.body: Viability depends on the thresholds below. {{unmet}} are not met today.

evidence.body: Every value used is marked as observed data, a derived estimate or an assumption, with its source where one exists.

validation.body: A simulation narrows uncertainty, it does not replace it. These points need checking against the real market.

report.downloadFailed: The report could not be generated.

compare.title: Comparison
compare.heading: Compare two versions
compare.description: Change the project, run the simulation again, and measure what actually moved.
compare.meaning: A higher index means the revised model holds up better across the scenarios that were run. It does not mean the business will succeed.
compare.noPrevious: This simulation has no earlier version to compare against.
compare.relaunchBody: A new run takes the project as it stands today and puts it through the same scenarios.

disclaimer.heading: Important
disclaimer.body: The results of this simulation are estimates based on the data, assumptions and scenarios available at the time of analysis. A high score guarantees neither viability, nor profitability, nor long-term survival.
disclaimer.bothWays: A low score does not mean the project is impossible either. These results are a decision-support tool, not a prediction.
disclaimer.short: Estimates from the simulated scenarios. Neither a guarantee nor a prediction.

notFound.heading: Page not found
notFound.body: This link does not match any page in the simulator.

understanding.baselineBody: These are the only values the deterministic engine uses. Everything else exists to establish them or to move them.
understanding.knowledge: What is known, and what is not
understanding.knowledgeBody: All four states are shown together: an assumption dressed as data would distort everything that follows.
understanding.evidenceBody: Every value carries where it came from and how confident the engine is in it.
understanding.pending: The project analysis is not available yet.

factors.heading: Discovered factors
factors.body: {{total}} factors identified for this sector. The list is not fixed — it follows the project being analysed.
factors.noEvidence: No source attached: this factor remains an assumption made by the engine.

scenarios.heading: Combinations tested
scenarios.body: Each scenario moves several factors at once: it is the combination that breaks a model, rarely a single factor.
scenarios.stressBody: The question here is not “how likely” but “at what point does it break”.
scenarios.survival: The model holds in {{percent}}% of scenarios

financials.heading: Financial trajectory
financials.body: A deterministic three-year projection, reproducible: same inputs, same numbers.
financials.sensitivityBody: What a single move changes on the index, every other lever held constant.
financials.conditionsBody: The thresholds the model has to clear for the scenarios to hold.
financials.pending: Financial results are not available yet.

lab.runningBody: Several agents are working on this analysis. It takes one to two minutes.
lab.notRun: This analysis has not been run yet. It builds on the simulation results rather than replacing them.
lab.needsRun: This analysis needs a completed simulation.

redTeam.heading: Attack my business
redTeam.body: Six roles look for where the project breaks. The point is not reassurance, it is finding what was not planned for.

customers.heading: Customer simulator
customers.body: A panel of synthetic customers reacts to your offer and your price. These are constructed profiles, not real people.
customers.curveLabel: Estimated revenue as a function of price

investors.heading: Investor simulator
investors.body: The case put in front of four profiles. What matters here are the objections — they are coming either way.
investors.prepare: To prepare before the first meeting

blackSwan.heading: Black swans
blackSwan.body: Rare but possible shocks, replayed through the same engine as the scenarios.
blackSwan.absorptionHint: Share of shocks the model survives without running out of cash.

universes.heading: Parallel universes
universes.body: The same project under other business models, run through the same scenarios.

timeMachine.heading: Time machine
timeMachine.body: The project projected over five years, one trajectory per scenario, with the point where they diverge.

experiments.heading: Experiments to run
experiments.body: What to go and check in the real world to turn assumptions into data.

timeline.noDivergence: No marked divergence over the horizon

signIn.heading: Sign in to continue
signIn.sharedAccount: Your IDEM account opens the simulator, the dashboard and iDeploy. There is no separate account to create.
signIn.documentTooLarge: Your document is too large to keep while you sign in — you will need to select it again when you come back.

reason.projects: Your IDEM projects belong to your account: sign in to find them here.
reason.analyse: The analysis runs on our servers, under your IDEM account. Sign in to start it — your document will be waiting here.
reason.launch: One last step: sign in to launch the simulation and keep its report.
